It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts. ### Execution model 1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows. 2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist: - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result) - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI) - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation 3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic. ### Key layers | Layer | Location | Purpose | |-------|----------|---------| | SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing | | Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) | | JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic | | Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic | | Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults | | Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents | | Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) | | Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup | ## GraalJS Constraints All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js. - Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals). - No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages. - No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`. - Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`. - Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo. - **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one. - Keep data structures JSON-safe. ## Running Tests Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed. ```bash # Run from the dmtools-agents repo root cd dmtools-agents # All tests dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json # Single test suite dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json ``` Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`). ### Writing tests for new logic **All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.** - Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_.js` file. - Add it to the corresponding `run_.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`. - Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module. - Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services. - Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config. - Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context. Example mock pattern: ```js var fileReadMock = function(opts) { var p = opts && (opts.path || opts); if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p]; if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; } }; ``` ### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring (preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible: 1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run --key value` patches the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden: ```bash dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \ --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \ --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \ --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \ --alwaysPostComments false \ --cleanupInputFolder false ``` 2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g. `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is project- and machine-specific): ```bash #!/bin/bash set -e mkdir -p outputs printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md ``` Rules for live e2e runs: - **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything via CLI overrides. - Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items. - Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input//` afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet. - After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`, `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather than trusting the job log. ## Conventions ### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE **This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite. Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages): - Company, customer, or product names - Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys - Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization - File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs - Sample data copied from real internal systems Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. # Publishes the archify machine-loop diagram (site/) to GitHub Pages.
# Repo Settings → Pages → Source = "GitHub Actions" (set 2026-09-21):
# nothing deploys until a workflow calls deploy-pages — this is it.
name: pages

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths: ['site/**', '.github/workflows/pages.yml']
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

concurrency:
  group: pages
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      # (the factory board moved to the dmtools-factory repo)
      - name: Stage site
        run: |
          mkdir -p _site
          rsync -a site/ _site/ --exclude 'index.visual-check*'

      - uses: actions/configure-pages@v5

      - uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3
        with:
          path: _site

      - id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4

content.text:
name: Agent Docs

# Mandatory check for PRs that touch agent configs, JS actions, instructions,
# prompts, snapshots or human docs:
#   1. Regenerates docs/agents/generated/* and snapshots/* and fails when the
#      committed files are stale (git diff non-empty).
#   2. Runs crap4dart similarity gate (v0.15.0) against .crap-baseline.json.
#   3. Runs the docs unit tests (agentDocGenerator + docs coverage) via dmtools.

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'
      - 'snapshots/**'
      - 'crap4dart.yaml'
      - '.crap-baseline.json'
      - '.github/workflows/agent-docs.yml'
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'
      - 'snapshots/**'
      - 'crap4dart.yaml'
      - '.crap-baseline.json'

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  docs-freshness:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '20'

      - name: Regenerate agent docs and prompt snapshots
        run: |
          node js/agentDocGenerator.js
          node generate_agent_snapshots.js

      - name: Fail when generated docs or snapshots are stale
        run: |
          if ! git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated snapshots; then
            echo "::error::docs/agents/generated or snapshots is stale. Run 'node js/agentDocGenerator.js && node generate_agent_snapshots.js' and commit the result."
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Run crap4dart similarity gate
        run: |
          curl -fsSL https://github.com/IstiN/crap4dart/releases/download/v0.15.0/crap4dart-linux-x64 \
            -o "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap4dart-linux-x64"
          chmod +x "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap4dart-linux-x64"
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap4dart-linux-x64" check --only similarity --baseline

  docs-coverage-tests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Install Java 17
        uses: actions/setup-java@v6
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: '17'

      - name: Install dmtools CLI
        run: |
          curl -fsSL https://github.com/epam/dm.ai/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash
          echo "$HOME/.dmtools/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Run docs unit tests
        run: |
          dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_agentDocsCoverage.json

### What changed
Cuts the machine-comment volume on PRs — measured on live #1387 (~8–9 comments per rework lap, ~1 with decision value) and, more importantly, stops the visible arm/red notices from leaking into every review/rework agent context build (~2.7 KB per build on #1387).

- **gh-808 finish line (L1)**: `buildGeneralCommentsSection` (the gh-1248 shared impl behind both `scm.js` and `githubHelpers.js`) now drops hidden `dmtools:` markers AND visible machine notices; a notices-only PR renders `null` (no empty header). `MACHINE_NOTICE_MARKERS` gains the two machine-read families that were missing: `🔴 red head ` (`redHeadMarkerLine`, re-read by `failMarkerState`) and `🔄 zombie re-dispatch ` (`validationLiveness`, re-read by `ZOMBIE_MARKER_RE`).
- **Notice dedup (L2)**: naked-pr-rearm (gh-1097) posts a one-line tail when a same-head gh-840 consume marker explains the nakedness — the marker payload stays byte-identical (dedup anchor + parsers read the marker, never the tail). Arm/red-gate arm notices append `(arm head xxxxxxx)` — the marker-prefix first line is untouched so the classifier key holds — and skip same-head repeats (fail-open on comment-read failure; a fresh head re-opens posting). Consume-audit (gh-840) tail is one short line.

### Key decisions
- The visible tails are human-only; EVERY machine contract stays in the hidden markers byte-for-byte — `latestRegistry` / verdict reconcile / gh-840 sweep / gh-957 lap guard / `alreadyRearmed` dedup are untouched.
- Repeat suppression keys on (anchored marker-prefix first line + head token): a repeat posts when the head changes or the red count advances; the red-gate budget semantics are unchanged.
- Labels rejected for this state (documented in #1391): lifecycle state already rides existing labels; the comments are audit evidence (gh-840/957/1097 each fix a live incident).
- L3 (summary + verdict + registry in one comment) and L4 (bound the registry repost — the dominant byte growth: 27 KB of #1387's 37 KB) stay open in #1391: posting-contract / evidence-model calls, deliberately not snuck into this PR.

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_machineNotice.json     # 22/0 (+7)
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_nakedPrReconcile.json  # 13/0 (+5, new manifest)
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_reworkConsumption.json # 31/0 (+1)
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json           # 819/0
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_reviewVerdicts.json    # 102/0
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_githubHelpers.json     # 150/0
```

Replay of the live #1387 timeline through the patched builders (sim scripts in the authoring repo, `audit/sim/pr-comment-reduction/`):
- agent-visible general comments **9 → 3** (only review summaries survive), section −2.7 KB per build;
- the same-head repeat 🧵 arm notice (6 min apart) is suppressed; consume audits ×4 and consume-explained re-arms ×2 shorten with byte-identical markers; the genuine first re-arm keeps its full text; different-head red-gate arms both still post.

<details>
<summary>Before → after, one lap of the cascade</summary>

| event | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| rework-consume | marker + 3-line legalese (334 B) | marker + 1 line (214 B) |
| naked-pr-rearm (consume-explained) | full story repeat (335 B) | one line (271 B) |

  sm: {
    runners: {
      bug: '.dmtools/runners/fa-bug-dev.json',
      story: '.dmtools/runners/fa-story-dev.json',

===
# SM kicker — thin stub over the canonical watchdog in the factory home.
# All logic (sm-liveness + head-completeness) lives in
# IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml.
# This repo's validation CI is `Quality` (display name "Quality") and its
# required context is the `crap` job.
name: SM kicker

run-name: '🥁 kicker ${{ github.event_name }} ${{ github.ref_name }}'

on:
  push:
    branches-ignore: [main]
  schedule:
    - cron: '13,43 * * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  actions: write
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read
  checks: read

concurrency:
  # dmtools-agents#682 (live fa#1202/#1203 2026-10-03, still reproducing
  # 2026-10-04 06:21–06:22 in THIS repo — runs 06:36/06:41/06:43): the
  # global group below already ran with cancel-in-progress:false, yet
  # kicker runs kept dying cancelled in chains. cancel-in-progress only
  # shields the RUNNING run — a queued run in the same group ALWAYS
  # supersedes (cancels) the pending one (GitHub docs: "Any existing
  # pending job or workflow in the same concurrency group, if it exists,
  # will be canceled and the new queued job or workflow will take its
  # place"). One global group meant every push anywhere (silent refresh,
  # factory-data snapshots, dev waves) cancelled every other branch's
  # pending kicker. Per-head-SHA group: no push can displace another
  # push's kicker — a queued kicker that is about to dispatch a tick
  # always gets to run (canonical fix + consumer notes: IstiN/
  # dmtools-agentic-workflows factory-sm-kicker.yml). Effective once the
  # canonical pin is bumped (separate PR): until then the called
  # workflow's own global group still supersedes.
  group: sm-kicker-${{ github.sha }}

content.text:
# Machine SM — thin stub over the FROZEN machine loop
# (IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows, reusable).
#
# Same freeze contract as dmtools-dart's machine-sm.yml: the workflow is
# pinned to an immutable SHA; agent code and the dmtools CLI resolve from
# RELEASES at run time via this repo's variables:
#   vars.AGENTS_VERSION  — dmtools-agents release tag ('latest' default)
#   vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION — dmtools-dart CLI release tag ('latest' default)
# Bump a version = repo-settings edit, never a workflow edit.
# NO caller-side concurrency: the factory owns the `machine-sm` group.

name: 'Machine SM'

run-name: >-
  🧹 SM ${{
    github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && 'manual tick' ||
    format('tick {0}', github.event.schedule || '') }}${{
  github.event.inputs.dryRun == 'true' && ' (dry)' || '' }}

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '*/10 * * * *'   # short ticks — the engine idles when busy
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      dryRun:
        description: 'Log the plan, perform no action'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: true

permissions:
  contents: write         # checkout + silent update-branch pushes
  issues: write           # labels + close-issue safety net
  pull-requests: write    # update-branch + merge
  checks: write           # bridge-free validation stamps
  actions: write          # workflow_dispatch on the teammate workflow

jobs:
  sm:
    # Pinned to the immutable SHA of IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows main
    # (the frozen machine-loop home; bump the SHA only together with the
    # matching loop change).
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@main
    with:
      # No .dmtools/config.js in this repo — the machine logins ride the
      # deployment-level input (#687, gh-728), exactly like the factory's
      # contract. Comma-separated LIST: the agent harness bot AND the CI
      # bot — github-actions[bot] authors its own PRs (live fa PR #1249)
      # and must ride the machine path (owner directive 2026-10-05).
      machine-author: 'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot],dmtools-factory-bot'
===
{
 "name": "JSRunner",
 "params": {
  "jsPath": "agents/js/machineSmAgent.js",
  "jobParams": {
   "repo": "epam/dmtools-dart",
   "scm": {
    "provider": "github"
   },
   "dryRun": false,
   "maxConcurrentRuns": 1,
   "maxReworkRounds": 2,
   "workflowFile": "ai-teammate.yml",
   "branchPrefix": "ai/gh-",
   "agentHandle": "ai-teammate",
   "issueLimit": 50
  }
 }
}

3. Register the actually-failing untracked check names into the tracked set on detection, then run the EXISTING bounded red-head rework flow (MAX_AUTO_REWORK_ROUNDS / 3-reds → park unchanged).
4. Config-first shortcut may ship as interim, but generic reconciliation is the acceptance bar.
5. Acceptance: green tracked verdict + failing untracked check → rework lap within one tick, bounded; fully-green PRs unchanged; failing check appears registered in the state JSON (auditable).

Now — "the reconcile job already fetches github_get_pr per PR". In smAgent.js, `prHeadAndLabels(repoInfo, prNumber)` fetches github_get_pr per PR — used by reconcile rules and reworkArmGate etc. But "the reconcile job" — in the MACHINE SM (machineSmAgent.js), `buildIssueState` → `provider.findPr` + `provider.prStatus(number)` — prStatus calls github_get_pr per PR. And its decision core reads checkConclusion + mergeState.

Which SM is "the SM" whose "check-tracker" has the blind spot? The factory-state JSON comes from smAgent.js (statePublish). Hmm — but "rework lap" derivation and MAX_AUTO_REWORK_ROUNDS... 

In smAgent.js: red-head cap (redHeadCapOf = 3) with the 🔴 markers — "the normal red-head rework flow" — that's `fail_validation` → report + red-head marker + requeue agent:rework, and the arm_rework rules (rework-on-red-gate-unlatched / rework-on-validation-failed) gated by redHeadCap. MAX_AUTO_REWORK_ROUNDS is the ai-teammate.yml workflow's env (the leg-side bound; machineSmAgent mirrors it as maxReworkRounds default 2).

In machineSmAgent.js: decideRedPrActions — 'CI red on PR #N' → dispatch rework; reworkExhausted (rounds >= maxReworkRounds) → needs-human label. That IS "MAX_AUTO_REWORK_ROUNDS"-bounded rework (the machine SM mirrors it).

And the machine SM's `pr` state carries `checkConclusion` AND `mergeState` — the ticket says "the PR's real mergeability (mergeStateStatus) is never reconciled against the tracked verdict". In machineSmAgent's decideActions:
- `checkConclusion === 'red'` → rework (bounded). 
- green + approved: mergeState BEHIND → updateBranch; CLEAN/mergeable → merge; BLOCKED → dispositionLoop; else skip.
- green + unapproved: review routing...

**IF checkConclusion is green but mergeState is UNSTABLE** (raw REST 'UNSTABLE' masked... wait — in the machineSM provider path, mergeState goes through `_ghOverrideMergeState` — on a fresh base UNSTABLE → masked 'CLEAN'! → the machine would try to MERGE an unmergeable PR (merge fails) every tick... or — `pr.mergeable === true` → merge attempt. The merge itself would fail (UNSTABLE = failing required check) — actually mergeable=true just means no conflict; the merge API would reject with required statuses failing. The machine SM merge fails each tick → frozen. THAT is a real blind spot in machineSmAgent.

Hmm wait — actually for #1392: checkConclusion would be RED (rollup includes docs-freshness failure)... IF the machine SM reconciled it. But #1392's issue (#1391) has NO machine labels → listMachineIssues filters it out → the machine SM never saw it. The sm_github.json SM handled it (PR-anchored rules). So for the sm_github SM: checkConclusion red + no matching rule (machine-only rework rules; review-stale-verdict needs green).

OK. Decision time. The ticket's prescribed fix targets THE SM whose input the factory JSON shows: "checks.verdict: success" — and says rework-on-red never fired because the input said green. The pre-baked context (ticket) is authoritative: implement the per-tick reconcile:

**For `pr_created` PRs whose tracked verdict is green but whose mergeStateStatus is UNSTABLE/FAILED → register the actually-failing check names into the tracked set → run the normal red-head rework flow (bounded).**

Given the architecture, the cleanest generic implementation matching the acceptance bar:

1. **A pure module** `js/common/mergeStateReconcile.js` (new): 
  - `unstableMergeStates()` → ['UNSTABLE', 'FAILED'] (also lowercase 'unstable'/'failed' normalization).
  - `trackedVerdictGreen(status)` → status.checkConclusion === 'green'.
  - `failingCheckNames(rollup)` → the actually-failing check names from the check-run rollup (FAILURE/TIMED_OUT, latest-per-context, bookeeping folded out — reuse the smProvider vocabulary).
  - `reconcileDecision(status, rollup)` → null when no reconcile applies (green PR, or mergeState not UNSTABLE/FAILED, or no failing checks found, or verdict already red/pending); otherwise { failingChecks: [names], mergeState, headSha, reason }.
   
2. **Wire into smAgent.js** — where? The tick's per-PR reconcile... The SM tick processes RULES; there's no generic per-PR reconcile hook other than rules. Hmm.

Wait — hold on. Let me reconsider: which "check-tracker" component computes the verdict the RULES see? smProvider.computePrStatus/checkConclusion — shared by BOTH SMs (smAgent's githubSource and machineSmAgent). The factory state JSON's checks record is separate (workflow-run based, factoryState.headVerdict).

The fix has two halves:
(a) **Rules' input**: make the query-side verdict red when the PR is truly unmergeable due to failing checks — i.e. reconcile mergeStateStatus against the tracked verdict in `computePrStatus`: when tally says green but the PR's raw mergeStateStatus is UNSTABLE/FAILED, downgrade checkConclusion to 'red' and attach the failing check names (from the rollup — the actually-failing checks GitHub sees). Then ALL existing red-keyed rules fire naturally: rework-on-red-gate-unlatched (machine PRs), review-stale-verdict (checks green → now excluded... hmm).

Wait, careful: downgrading checkConclusion to red would make review-stale-verdict NOT fire (it wants green). For the human PR #1392 the desired outcome per the ticket is a REWORK LAP. rework-on-red-gate-unlatched is machine-only → wouldn't fire for ajaxspace's PR. Hmm — but "rework-on-red-ci" in the ticket's words arms "agent:rework on the issue either by the review verdict (CHANGES_REQUESTED) or by red pre-merge CI"... the rule description says prMachineAuthor: auto rework fires ONLY on machine-authored PRs (owner rule). Hmm, so for the live PR #1392 (human-authored), what SHOULD the machine do after the reconcile makes it red? Per the red-head flow: report + requeue agent:rework on the linked issue — machine-only? fail_validation for guest PRs = park (validation_failed). Hmm.

But wait — the live PR #1392's rework lap WAS machine-driven (agent:rework armed at 09:45 from the CHANGES_REQUESTED verdict — the review leg labels agent:rework on the ISSUE carrier regardless of authorship; "The review leg itself labels agent:rework for CHANGES_REQUESTED verdicts" — per decideGreenUnapprovedActions comment: "The review leg itself labels agent:rework for CHANGES_REQUESTED verdicts"). And rework-on-red-ci (the dispatch rule) keys on the ISSUE label agent:rework + notPrLabels agent:rework + prMachineAuthor... hmm no — rework-on-red-ci's query HAS prMachineAuthor: true. Hmm, but the lap ran for ajaxspace's PR at 23:5x...

The dispatch could have come from rework-unresolved-threads (machine-only) — no. From rework-on-label (PR label agent:rework)? The PR events show label adds at 09:45:04/05 and unlabeled at 00:08:37. Maybe agent:rework was ON THE PR (added by the review leg at 09:45, together with ai_pr_reviewed) — rework-on-label has NO prMachineAuthor gate ("Manual rework request: agent:rework label on the PR itself -> rework on demand, ANY author"). So the machine reworked the human PR because the REVIEW leg armed it via the PR carrier.

So the loop for a reviewed PR with CHANGES_REQUESTED: review leg arms agent:rework (PR carrier) → lap runs → fixes pushed → lap consumed the label → verdict now stale → review-stale-verdict should re-review (checks green required!) → docs-freshness red → no re-review, no re-arm → FROZEN.

# Machine SM factory leg — REUSABLE workflow (dmtools-agentic-workflows:
# the frozen machine-loop home. GitHub requires reusable workflows at the
# .github/workflows root — no subdirectories).
#
# Migrated from IstiN/dmtools-agents factory-sm.yml (f377609) — the
# agents-repo copy is DEPRECATED for new callers (kept only so existing
# pinned users like fa keep resolving their historical SHA).
#
# FREEZE CONTRACT: target repositories carry only a thin stub (schedule +
# this call) pinned to an immutable SHA of THIS repo. Agent code and the
# dmtools CLI are NOT tied to that SHA anymore — they resolve from RELEASES
# by version knobs (repo variables of the CALLER, per-repo, no workflow
# edits to bump):
#
#   vars.AGENTS_VERSION   — dmtools-agents release tag ('latest' or e.g.
#                           'agents-rel-20260928-…'); the agent pack
#                           (sm_github) is fetched from that release's
#                           asset catalog via the dmtools registry
#                           (DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY). Default: latest.
#   vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION  — dmtools-dart CLI release tag ('latest' or
#                           'vX.Y.Z'); installed from the release bundle.
#                           Default: latest.
#
# Runs in the CALLER's context: github.repository = the target repo,
# vars.* and secrets.* resolve from the caller (each target pins its own
# versions).
#
# What it does: resolves the two version knobs, installs the dmtools CLI
# (release asset, no repo file needed), then runs the SM rule engine as a
# VERSIONED AGENT PACK (dmtools run sm_github@latest) against the target
# repo's loop state — the pack carries smAgent.js + rules + engine closure,
# verified against the release's sha256 inventory.
#
# Caller stub:
#   on:
#     schedule: [{cron: '*/10 * * * *'}]
#     workflow_dispatch: {inputs: {dryRun: {type: boolean, default: true}}}
#   permissions:
#     # A reusable workflow CANNOT grant itself permissions the caller did
#     # not issue (GitHub hard rule) — the stub must pre-grant everything
#     # the SM needs:
#     #   contents: write       checkout + silent update-branch pushes
#     #   issues: write         labels + close-issue safety net
#     #   pull-requests: write  update-branch + merge
#     #   checks: write         bridge-free validation stamps
#     # NEVER add `workflows: write` — it is NOT a valid permissions scope
#     # for GITHUB_TOKEN and makes the workflow file UNPARSEABLE (live
#     # fah#1717: HTTP 422 "Unexpected value 'workflows'", SM dead until
#     # reverted). GITHUB_TOKEN can never push workflow-file changes no
#     # matter what the stub declares.
#   jobs:
#     sm:
#       uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@<ref>
#       secrets:
#         # Silent updates that carry main's workflow-file changes need a
#         # workflows-capable PAT: pass it here (the factory resolves
#         # inputs.silent-token || secrets.SILENT_GH_TOKEN || github.token;
#         # the with-input channel cannot reference secrets — 422).
#         SILENT_GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.PAT_TOKEN }}
#       uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@<ref>
#       with:
#         dryRun: ${{ github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false' }}   # STRING —
#         # typed (boolean) reusable inputs reject expressions; strings take them.
#       secrets:
#         SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}

name: 'Factory · Machine SM'

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      runner:
        description: 'Runner label (self-hosted pools must be visible to the CALLING org)'
        type: string
        default: 'ubuntu-slim'
      dryRun:
        description: "'true' to log the plan without acting (STRING — boolean-typed reusable inputs cannot take expressions, live bisect probes D/E)"
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'false'
      machine-author:
        description: "Deployment's machine (bot) login for #687 PR rules: excluded from review-external-once, gates rework re-arm in PR-anchored reviews and the SM prMachineAuthor rules (auto legs, e.g. auto rework). Global-level knob — the agents repo carries no hardcoded login."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      silent-token:
        description: "The caller's github.token for silent branch updates (#687) — pushes with it trigger no workflows. Routed as an INPUT: GitHub delivers an EMPTY value when github.token is mapped through the reusable-call secrets block (live-verified), while inputs carry it; GitHub auto-masks token values in logs either way."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      ci-workflow:
        description: "CI workflow FILE NAME the SM dispatches on PR heads (dispatch-only CI: pushes fire no CI). Per-repo knob — e.g. 'quality.yml' (dmtools-dart) vs 'ci.yml' (fa). Rides jobParams.ciWorkflow into the SM engine."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'quality.yml'
      validation-checks:
        description: "Bridge-free mode (factory #510): the tick stamps these check names itself. JSON array as a STRING (e.g. '[\"agents-suite\",\"static\",\"gate\"]')."
        required: false
        type: string

# SM kicker — thin stub over the canonical watchdog in the factory home.
# All logic (sm-liveness + head-completeness) lives in
# IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml.
# This repo's validation CI is `Quality` (display name "Quality") and its
# required context is the `crap` job.
name: SM kicker

run-name: '🥁 kicker ${{ github.event_name }} ${{ github.ref_name }}'

on:
  push:
    branches-ignore: [main]
  schedule:
    - cron: '13,43 * * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  actions: write
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read
  checks: read

concurrency:
  # dmtools-agents#682 (live fa#1202/#1203 2026-10-03, still reproducing
  # 2026-10-04 06:21–06:22 in THIS repo — runs 06:36/06:41/06:43): the
  # global group below already ran with cancel-in-progress:false, yet
  # kicker runs kept dying cancelled in chains. cancel-in-progress only
  # shields the RUNNING run — a queued run in the same group ALWAYS
  # supersedes (cancels) the pending one (GitHub docs: "Any existing
  # pending job or workflow in the same concurrency group, if it exists,
  # will be canceled and the new queued job or workflow will take its
  # place"). One global group meant every push anywhere (silent refresh,
  # factory-data snapshots, dev waves) cancelled every other branch's
  # pending kicker. Per-head-SHA group: no push can displace another
  # push's kicker — a queued kicker that is about to dispatch a tick
  # always gets to run (canonical fix + consumer notes: IstiN/
  # dmtools-agentic-workflows factory-sm-kicker.yml). Effective once the
  # canonical pin is bumped (separate PR): until then the called
  # workflow's own global group still supersedes.
  group: sm-kicker-${{ github.sha }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  kicker:
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml@main
    with:
      sm_workflow: machine-sm.yml
      ci_workflow: quality.yml
      ci_display_name: Quality
      required_contexts: crap

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      runner:
        description: 'Runner label for the kicker jobs (e.g. ubuntu-slim, ubuntu-latest, or custom self-hosted label)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'ubuntu-slim'
      sm_workflow:
        description: 'File name of the Machine SM workflow in the caller repo'
        type: string
        default: 'machine-sm.yml'
      ci_workflow:
        description: 'File name of the validation CI workflow to dispatch'
        type: string
        default: 'ci.yml'
      ci_display_name:
        description: 'Workflow display NAME as it appears in the runs API'
        type: string
        default: 'CI'
      required_contexts:
        description: 'Comma-separated required check context names'
        type: string
        default: 'Quality gate,JS engine integration (quickjs-ng),Binaries smoke gate'
    secrets:
      APP_ID:
        description: 'Optional GitHub App id (awf#52). With APP_PRIVATE_KEY set, kicker API calls ride a per-job App installation token instead of github.token. Absent => github.token, byte-identical to today.'
        required: false
      APP_PRIVATE_KEY:
        description: 'Private key (PEM) of the APP_ID GitHub App.'
        required: false
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      runner:
        description: 'Runner label for the kicker jobs'
        type: string
        default: 'ubuntu-slim'
      sm_workflow:
        description: 'SM workflow file'
        type: string
        default: 'machine-sm.yml'
      ci_workflow:
        description: 'CI workflow file to dispatch'
        type: string
        default: 'ci.yml'
      ci_display_name:
        description: 'CI workflow display name'
        type: string
        default: 'CI'
      required_contexts:
        description: 'Comma-separated required check contexts'
        type: string
        default: 'Quality gate,JS engine integration (quickjs-ng),Binaries smoke gate'

permissions:
  actions: write        # workflow_dispatch: sm / ci
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read
  checks: read

concurrency:
  # Per-head-SHA group (dmtools-agents#682, live fa#1202/#1203 on
  # 2026-10-03 23:05–23:57; still reproducing 2026-10-04 06:21–06:22 —
  # eight branches' kicker runs cancelled inside one 36-second dev-wave,
  # fa run ids 37182568709…37182598010). The fa #911 fix below stopped
  # the IN-FLIGHT kills, but the global group kept killing the PENDING
  # ones: a queued run in a shared concurrency group ALWAYS supersedes
  # the pending one ("Any existing pending job or workflow in the same
  # concurrency group, if it exists, will be canceled and the new queued
  # job or workflow will take its place" — GitHub docs);
  # cancel-in-progress: false only shields the RUNNING run. So every
  # silent-refresh push / factory-data snapshot / dev-wave push cancelled
  # every other branch's pending kicker, the required contexts
  # (sm-liveness/head-completeness where a repo requires them) ended
  # CANCELLED on fresh PR heads, and the PRs sat BLOCKED until manual
  # reruns (2 dead zones + 2 manual reruns on 2026-10-03 alone).
  # Scoping the group to the pushed head SHA means no push can displace
  # another push's kicker: a queued kicker that is about to dispatch a
  # tick ALWAYS gets to run. The kicker jobs stay seconds-cheap and
  # idempotent (liveness re-probes before dispatching, head-completeness
  # re-checks with a 45s grace), so wave-time parallel kickers are
  # harmless — same cost posture as the fa #911 "let them queue" call.
  # cancel-in-progress stays false: even a same-SHA collision (schedule
  # + manual dispatch on one commit) must never kill an in-flight kicker.
  # CONSUMERS: re-pin your stub to this commit. If your stub defines its
  # OWN caller-level concurrency group, scope it per-head too (or drop
  # it — this group now carries the scoping): a caller-level global
  # group re-introduces the pending-run supersession on its own.
  group: factory-sm-kicker-${{ github.sha }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
  SM_WORKFLOW: ${{ inputs.sm_workflow || 'machine-sm.yml' }}
  CI_WORKFLOW: ${{ inputs.ci_workflow || 'ci.yml' }}
  CI_DISPLAY: ${{ inputs.ci_display_name || 'CI' }}
  REQUIRED_CONTEXTS: ${{ inputs.required_contexts || 'Quality gate,JS engine integration (quickjs-ng),Binaries smoke gate' }}

machine-author: 'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot],dmtools-factory-bot'
      # This repo dispatches no CI on PR heads (docs checks only) — the SM
      # leaves validation to the event-driven merge bot and labels.
      ci-workflow: ''
      # Manual ticks default to dry; cron ticks run live.
      dryRun: ${{ github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false' }}
      # Factory-state snapshot → factory-data branch (board: site/factory,
      # third tab; fa machine-sm.yml parity — transport lives in
      # js/factoryState.js, publishing is opt-in per factory).
      # gh-1108: tokensAsset pins the agents factory's OWN tokens stream —
      # fetchTokensFromBranch defaults to the fixed fa-side asset, so
      # without this knob the agents tick would fetch (and silently
      # publish) the WRONG factory's rows on any shared branch.
      state-publish: '{"channel":"release","tag":"factory-data","asset":"agents-state.json","tokensAsset":"agents-tokens.json"}'
      # Silent branch updates: input channel (github.token via secrets/in
      # blocks arrives empty through a reusable call — live-verified).
      silent-token: ${{ github.token }}
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      # App auth (awf#52): minted installation token wins over the PAT
      # inside the factory when both secrets are present.
      APP_ID: ${{ secrets.APP_ID }}
      APP_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
      SILENT_GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SILENT_GH_TOKEN }}

* rest of the agent ecosystem uses — so the watchdog runs unchanged on any
 * forge the bridge supports. The one exception today is GitHub's
 * update-branch (no native tool yet) which falls back to the gh CLI.
 *
 * Provider contract (all methods):
 *   listMachineIssues(machineLabels, agentHandle, limit) → [{number, title, labels, assignees}]
 *       Open issues carrying any machine label or the agent assignee.
 *   findPr(issueNumber, branchPrefix) → null | {number, state, branch}
 *       OPEN first (branch match <prefix><n> or body references #n), then
 *       MERGED on the branch (close-issue safety net).
 *   prStatus(prNumber) → {state, checkConclusion, mergeState, mergeable, author}
 *       checkConclusion: 'red' | 'green' | 'pending' | 'none'.
 *       author: creator login ('' when the API does not expose it) — the
 *       prMachineAuthor gate keys on it.
 *   activeMachineRuns() → [issueNumber, …]
 *       Issues with a queued/in_progress machine run right now.
 *   dispatchLeg(issueNumber, leg, reason)
 *       Fire the machine runner for that issue (leg: dev/review/rework).
 *   updateBranch(prNumber) / merge(prNumber) / closeIssue(n, comment)
 *   addIssueLabel(issueNumber, label)
 *
 * Known gaps (documented, non-fatal):
 *   - gitlab has no close-issue tool — closeIssue warns and no-ops.
 *   - gitlab activeMachineRuns cannot map a pipeline to an issue number
 *     (pipelines do not expose trigger variables) — any running API-sourced
 *     pipeline counts as "machine busy" (conservative: fewer parallel legs).
 *   - gitlab exposes no machine verdict records (gh-807: no MR-note reader
 *     in the tool catalog yet) — latestVerdictRecord is absent, so the
 *     latestVerdict/notLatestVerdict query guards never match/fail-open and
 *     the reconciliation stays GitHub-machine-loop behavior for now.

content.text:
===== review-stale-verdict
GitHub PR: CHANGES_REQUESTED verdict pinned to an older commit (fixes pushed after the review) + green -> re-arm agent:review. review-on-label dispatches the runner, the runner consumes the label and re-reviews the current head; the fresh verdict's commit_id equals the head, so this never loops. Never on approved PRs (pr_approved is sticky — approved rework re-validates, never re-reviews). agent:rework excluded (#683, 2026-10-04): the ONLY re-review armer that can overlap rework-unresolved-threads (a stale CHANGES_REQUESTED with open threads) — a PR sent to rework must not simultaneously arm a re-review; review-threads-resolved re-arms the review once the threads are resolved. workflowRef={branch}: the leg runs on the PR head — GitHub links the run to the PR (visible in PR checks/timeline as the review/rework run).
===== review-threads-resolved
GitHub PR: all review threads resolved + the last verdict is older than the head (fixes landed and the threads were worked through) + green -> re-arm agent:review. Covers PR #676: the rework resolves threads (the CHANGES_REQUESTED verdict dissolves into COMMENTED), so verdict-staleness alone misses it. Convergent: the re-review's verdict lands on the current head and its fresh threads are unresolved until worked. Never on approved PRs (pr_approved is sticky — approved rework re-validates, never re-reviews). workflowRef={branch}: the leg runs on the PR head — GitHub links the run to the PR (visible in PR checks/timeline as the review/rework run).

import json, collections

with open('sm_github.json') as f:
    d = json.load(f, object_pairs_hook=collections.OrderedDict)

rules = d['params']['jobParams']['rules']
patched = []
for r in rules:
    rid = r.get('id')
    q = r.get('query') or {}
    if rid in ('review-stale-verdict', 'review-threads-resolved') and q.get('checks') == 'green':
        # gh-140: gate on the TRACKED-set verdict, not the effective one —
        # an untracked failing check must not freeze the re-review armer.
        newq = collections.OrderedDict()
        for k, v in q.items():
            if k == 'checks':
                newq['trackedChecks'] = 'green'
            else:
                newq[k] = v
        r['query'] = newq
        r['description'] = r.get('description', '') + \
            ' gh-140: gates on trackedChecks (the tracked-set verdict), not the effective fold — ' \
            'an untracked failing check (mergeStateStatus UNSTABLE, live #1392 docs-freshness) reds ' \
            'the effective verdict so the red-head flow owns it, while the machine\'s own validation ' \
            'stayed green — exactly the head a re-review may re-enter; a tracked red still blocks.'
        patched.append(rid)

with open('sm_github.json', 'w') as f:
    json.dump(d, f, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False)
    f.write('\n')
print('patched:', patched)
EOF

          "source": "github",

          "workflowRef": "{branch}"
        },
        {
          "description": "GitHub PR: validated + reviewed (both latches) + ANY verdict pinned to an older commit + all review threads worked + the head has NO concluded checks (a push moved it after the review — silent-update/rework — so the rollup reads 'none' and every green-gated review path skips) -> RE-REVIEW FIRST (owner 2026-09-29: after ai_validated + a review, a moved head re-runs the REVIEW, never the validation; the single pre-merge validation stays in validate-armed, post-approve, on the final head). Convergent: the fresh verdict's commit_id equals the head, so staleVerdict clears — never loops. raw = raw.replace(d_old2, d_new2)

open('sm_github.json', 'w').write(raw)
print('ok')
EOF

content.text:
# gh-1400: [fix] SM check-tracker blind spot: failing checks outside the tracked set (docs-freshness) leave a PR silently unmergeable — rework-on-red never fires

## Description

Observed live on PR #1392 (2026-11-06/07): the rework lap fixed all 6 review findings (suite 8996/0), the tracked `verdict` check (Quality) went **green** at 00:03 — and the PR froze. GitHub's real `mergeStateStatus` is **UNSTABLE** because the `docs-freshness` check (a separate workflow) fails on the new head. The SM tick (01:15, factory-state JSON) shows the PR parked in `pr_created` with `checks.verdict: success` — **the rework-on-red rules never fire because their input says green**. No lap for ~12h and counting.

## Root cause

The SM's check-tracker monitors a fixed set of workflows (Quality/verdict runs). Any failing check **outside that set** is invisible: the PR's real mergeability (`mergeStateStatus`) is never reconciled against the tracked verdict, so `rework-on-red-ci` / red-head counters see nothing to react to.

## Fix direction

1. **Reconcile per tick** (the reconcile job already calls `github_get_pr` per PR — the `mergeStateStatus` is in that response): for `pr_created` PRs whose tracked verdict is green but whose `mergeStateStatus` is UNSTABLE/FAILED, register the actually-failing check names into the tracked set and run the normal red-head rework flow (bounded by MAX_AUTO_REWORK_ROUNDS).
2. Or simpler config-first step: add `docs-freshness` (and any repo-required checks) to the tracked check list.
3. Keep the red-head cap semantics unchanged (3 reds → park → needs-human).

## Acceptance

1. Replay: PR with green tracked verdict + failing untracked check → rework lap derived within one tick (bounded).
2. No change for fully-green PRs; red-head cap still parks after 3.
3. The SM state JSON shows the failing check registered (auditable).

### What changed
Closed the SM check-tracker blind spot (live #1392: tracked Quality green, untracked `docs-freshness` failing, mergeStateStatus UNSTABLE → PR froze ~12h with no rework lap). The per-PR reconcile (`smProvider.computePrStatus`) now downgrades the effective verdict to `red` when the PR body reports `mergeStateStatus` UNSTABLE/FAILED while the check-runs fold reads green/none — the existing bounded red-head flow (`fail-validation`, `rework-on-red-gate-unlatched`) reacts within one tick, caps unchanged.

### Key decisions
- New pure module `js/common/mergeStateReconcile.js` (no requires — smProvider/factoryState require it, never back): latest-per-context failure census, machine bookkeeping stamps folded out, BLOCKED deliberately excluded (it's the gh-828 conversation gate, not a check failure).
- The two re-review armers (`review-stale-verdict`, `review-threads-resolved`) now gate on `trackedChecks: 'green'` (the pre-reconcile fold, new `trackedVerdict` status field) — an untracked red must freeze the REWORK flow, not the re-review economy. `review-stale-verdict-unchecked` keeps the effective `checks: 'none'` (a commit-status failure reds it → red-head flow owns the head).
- AC3 audit: the status and the factory-state cards carry `untrackedFailingChecks`/`untrackedFailing` (names + failed-run links) + raw `mergeStateStatus`; fully-green and tracked-red payloads gain no reconcile keys.

Completion guard passes — 4 commits landed ahead of `origin/main`, tree clean. All verification is done; final summary:

## gh-1400 — SM check-tracker blind spot: closed

**Root cause** (live PR #1392): the check-tracker's fold saw only the tracked Quality run (green), while `docs-freshness` failed on the same head — GitHub's real `mergeStateStatus` read UNSTABLE, merge lanes refused it, and every lane keyed on the tracked verdict said green. No rework lap for ~12h.

**Fix** — 4 production pieces, all TDD-covered:
1. **`js/common/mergeStateReconcile.js`** (new pure module): when the fold reads green/none but the PR *reports* UNSTABLE/FAILED, the verdict downgrades to `red` and the failing checks are registered (latest-per-context census, bookkeeping stamps folded out, BLOCKED excluded — it's the gh-828 conversation gate).
2. **`smProvider.computePrStatus`**: reconcile rides the `github_get_pr` response already fetched (no new probe); status carries `trackedVerdict` + `untrackedFailingChecks` + raw `mergeStateStatus`.
3. **`githubSource`**: new `trackedChecks` query guard + `needsStatus` wiring — the two re-review armers (`review-stale-verdict`, `review-threads-resolved`) in `sm_github.json` now gate on the tracked fold so an untracked red never freezes them; the red-head consumers (`fail-validation`, `rework-on-red-gate-unlatched`) keep the effective verdict and react within one tick, caps/parks unchanged.
4. **`factoryState`** (AC3): cards on unstable-but-green-cited heads register `untrackedFailing` (names + failed-run links) + `mergeStateStatus` in the state JSON.

**Verification**: new `test_mergeStateReconcile.js` (40 tests) — including the true live shape (failure invisible to the check-runs API → census empty, mergeStateStatus is the registration), negative cases (BLOCKED/CLEAN/red-fold/pending-fold never reconcile), and combination cases. Full suite against the frozen tree: **9034 passed, 0 failed**. The tests caught and fixed 3 real defects during the loop (constant-name typo, fixture `event` field, item-shape assertion).
